title: Walk a class hierarchy

blocks.text: Java has no single call for a full hierarchy. `getSuperclass()` gives one parent, and returns **`null` for `Object`, interfaces, primitives and `void`**. `getInterfaces()` gives only the interfaces a type **declares directly**: interfaces reached through a superclass or through a super-interface are not in it.

items: `superclasses(type)`: `type`, then its parent, then that parent's parent, until `getSuperclass()` returns `null`.
`allInterfaces(type)`: every interface `type` has, those declared on **any superclass** and every **super-interface** of those, each once. The order is not graded.

blocks.text: With `Shape implements Drawable`, `Scalable extends Resizable` and `Circle extends Shape implements Scalable`:

cases.says: superclasses(Circle) is [Circle, Shape, Object]; for a class implementing one interface directly, allInterfaces is that interface.
A class whose parent implements Drawable has Drawable among its interfaces.
A class implementing Scalable, which extends Resizable, has both; Circle has all three.
superclasses of an interface, of int and of Object is the type alone.

concepts: The full hierarchy is walked with getSuperclass() until it returns null, which it does for Object, interfaces, primitives and void.
getInterfaces() returns only directly declared interfaces, so all interfaces need a recursive walk over superclasses and super-interfaces.
